# 4/7/26
*[[Killian]], [[Abraham]], [[Niklas Natt|Niklas]]*
*S7D1*

We head over to [[Sigrund Hierta|Sigrund]]'s newsroom. He's deep in thought at his desk and doesn't acknowledge us. I walk up and knock obnoxiously on his desk.

I ask him about the Stockholm opera scene and specifically about [[Sverker]]. He says opera isn't his forte, but he had heard about a different death connected to the [[Royal Opera]] — not a singer, someone less famous, so the name didn't stick. He doesn't know the details. He notes that Stockholm is chaotic right now: people are unhappy with the government, the new police force is struggling, and the mix of wealth and poverty is creating tension. He recommends we pick up a copy of the City Gazette when we arrive — it'll give us good background on current happenings. He'll dig up what he can about the other death and telegraph us at the Golden Peace.

I ask about a local contact who knows the scene. He warns us away from his counterpart at the Stockholm paper — a sleazy bastard. Instead, he recommends [[Erik Johan Stagnelius]], a poet and actor with a permanent residence at the [[Golden Peace]] hotel. He's deeply embedded in the Stockholm arts scene and was one of [[Sverker]]'s closest friends. Sigrund says he and Erik go back to childhood in Uppsala.

He also suggests we stop at the inn for ginger tea before the journey — it helps with motion sickness on the steam train.

We stop at the inn, get our tea to go, and board the train. Before it departs, we're each handed the latest issue of the City Gazette.

On the train, [[Abraham]] tells us about his Danish author friend [[Franzibald Hansen]], who writes about Norse mythology. Hansen had been visiting [[Linnea Elfeklint|Linnea]] and learned through her that Abraham was connected to the Society. He left a note with [[Algot Frisk|Algot]] for Abraham: he also has the Sight and is working with the Society. He also left Abraham a piece of jewelry with a green gemstone that he wants researched. Abraham has been skimming through Norse mythology texts looking for references to jewelry featuring a green gemstone, and he's focusing his investigation on whether the stone is jade or emerald.

Reading the City Gazette, we find several relevant articles:

- Almost a month after the murder of [[Sverker]] von Essen — star tenor of the [[Royal Opera]]'s production of Verdi's *A Masked Ball* — the police have no suspects. Police Commissioner [[Gabriel Utterson]] issued a statement from the new headquarters on Coyne Street promising justice. The understudy [[Rufus Holberg]] has announced he will continue the production in Sverker's memory.
- The conductor of the [[Royal Opera]], [[Mortimer Cronstedt]], died six weeks ago after consuming turtle soup at the [[Golden Peace]] tavern. Rumors of botulism are circulating. [[Niklas Natt|Niklas]] notes this and wants to find out if anyone took out life insurance on him.
- [[Professor Liebholz]] at [[Bern's Salon]] is presenting an evening of spirits and ghostly visions — one pound admission, three for a numbered seat. Worth investigating.

We arrive at Stockholm's newly constructed central station. The city is bustling — a stark contrast to the stillness of Uppsala. Travelers, servants, day laborers, beggars, carriages, and cattle crowd the streets.

A shiny black coach stops in front of us. A skinny man in a top hat sits in the coachman's seat — [[Karl-Axel Trygg]], [[August T. Lysander|Lysander]]'s valet. An elegantly dressed man with a well-groomed beard and pince-nez steps out: [[August T. Lysander]]. He's pleased to meet us in person and offers to take us wherever we need — the police headquarters or the hotel to freshen up. We opt for the hotel.

We travel across the bridge to the [[Town Between Bridges]]. Along the way, Lysander points out the police headquarters just as we cross onto the island, and the National Archives on a neighboring island — a useful resource, he says. He tells us about the rumors circulating in Stockholm:

- The turtle soup death at the Golden Peace is the talk of the city. The conductor was well-known in high circles, so it made the papers. As far as anyone knows, only one person died from it.
- A disease in the [[Whitehill]] district is causing at least one death per day. Doctors are working on it but it hasn't spread beyond the slums yet.
- He called us here because he believes a vaesen is responsible for the murders. He's been fascinated with vaesen since childhood and believes they live among us — that humans and vaesen can coexist if treated with respect. Something in his gut tells him no human could have done this. The police commissioner, a close friend, has shared the gruesome details with him, and it doesn't sound like anything a person could do. He wants us to find the vaesen and understand why it's killing — not destroy it, but resolve whatever is driving it.

I ask why he's so certain it's a vaesen. He says the killings are too gruesome, the police have found nothing — no clues, no leads — and humans make mistakes. He acknowledges Jack the Ripper happened nine years ago, but this feels different.

I ask if there's been any confirmed vaesen activity in Stockholm recently. He doesn't know of any, but says the commissioner will have everything the police know.

I ask about occultists in town who might have insight. He recommends [[Sigrid]] at the National Archives — not an occultist herself, but very knowledgeable, has worked there for years, and can point us to relevant historical texts and objects. She doesn't like people, so we'll need to get on her good side. Money goes a long way in this city.

He tells us he'll be at his factory if we need him, and that our accommodations at the Golden Peace — rooms and meals — are covered. He advises us not to bring up the turtle soup with the tavernkeeper.

We check into the [[Golden Peace]]. Our rooms are on the second floor — a bit drafty but clean. The tavern on the ground floor has windows facing the East Long Street quay, ceramic stoves, tea lights, and guests in armchairs and at white-clothed tables. It's around noon.

We sit down for lunch. Abraham orders the yellow pea soup. Niklas orders the meatball soup. I order the turtle soup — and the roasted mutton. We get a bottle of the house red.

Looking around the tavern, we notice a short man at a corner table — blunt hair, pointed nose, head tilted to one side, speaking loudly and gesturing broadly while reciting poetry to his tablemate. Almost certainly [[Erik Johan Stagnelius]].

I take my turtle soup and wander over. As I approach, I catch him mid-poem:

*"Haste, oh be lovely bride, who ready our lonely lovers' couch, by the world rejected by God set aside. Thou art my only hope."*

He looks up and calls me a fellow patron of the arts. I tell him the poem was almost as delicious as the soup I'm enjoying. He invites us to sit. I motion Abraham and Niklas over and introduce us. I mention that we have a mutual acquaintance — [[Sigrund Hierta|Sigrund]] the reporter from Uppsala. Erik lights up: *"What a great man. We go back a while — I'm originally from Uppsala, we've known each other since we were young children."*

[[Abraham]] recites one of his own published poems. Erik is visibly impressed — he recognizes it and applauds. He's delighted to learn Abraham is the author, and even more excited when Abraham mentions he's working on a novel in a new genre: a thriller with supernatural elements. Erik calls it both interesting and terrifying, and asks for a copy when it's published.

We tell Erik we're in Stockholm to help investigate [[Sverker]]'s murder. His demeanor shifts completely — he slumps, goes quiet, and says Sverker was a true artist. *"Always smelled so lovely of lavender."* They spent many nights here after performances, reciting poems and singing until early morning.

Erik tells us there were only two people he could think of who held ill will toward Sverker:

- The opera's conductor and staff had decided that Sverker had run his course in *A Masked Ball* and were planning to bring in his understudy as lead. Sverker was furious and had no intention of stepping aside. That may have made him a target.
- The conductor is dead now, so he couldn't have done it. But the understudy — [[Rufus Holberg]] — is still around. Erik thinks it's obvious he should be a suspect, though the police aren't pointing at anyone. He occasionally comes to the [[Golden Peace]] but mostly stays away. Erik says he doesn't know Rufus well, but anything is possible.

I ask if he gives any credence to the rumor that something supernatural is involved. He laughs and says he only believes in that stuff for his poetry.

[[Abraham]] asks whether he's ever noticed that some people seem too rich to have accumulated their wealth in one lifetime, or that ruling-class families look the same across generations. Erik stares blankly. He spits at the mention of the English and says he always assumed it was inbreeding.

Erik excuses himself — years of drinking have caught up with him. He carefully makes his way upstairs.

---

*Advantages for this mystery: [[Abraham]] +2 Investigation (connection to [[Franzibald Hansen]]); [[Killian]] +2 Investigation (contact with [[Erik Johan Stagnelius]]); [[Niklas Natt|Niklas]] +2 Investigation (read the Codex before departing).*

*1 XP awarded (session participation).*

## Summary 4/7/26

**Objective:** Investigate the murder of tenor [[Sverker]] von Essen at the [[Royal Opera]], Stockholm. [[August T. Lysander]] believes a vaesen is responsible.

**Key info:**
- [[Sverker]] was being replaced by understudy [[Rufus Holberg]] — he refused to step aside. [[Erik Johan Stagnelius]] names Rufus as prime suspect.
- Conductor [[Mortimer Cronstedt]] also dead — turtle soup at the [[Golden Peace]], ~6 weeks ago. Niklas wants to check for life insurance.
- Police have no leads. Commissioner [[Gabriel Utterson]] is a close friend of Lysander — good contact.
- [[Sigrid]] at the National Archives can help with research but dislikes people; bribery works.
- [[Professor Liebholz]] is running a ghost show at [[Bern's Salon]] — worth a visit.
- Abraham has a green gemstone jewelry piece left by [[Franzibald Hansen]] (has the Sight, works with the Society) to research.

**New NPCs:** [[Erik Johan Stagnelius]], [[Rufus Holberg]], [[Gabriel Utterson]], [[Mortimer Cronstedt]], [[Sigrid]], [[Professor Liebholz]], [[Karl-Axel Trygg]], [[Franzibald Hansen]]

**New locations:** [[Golden Peace]] (base), [[Town Between Bridges]], [[Bern's Salon]]


# 4/14/26
*[[Killian]], [[Abraham]], [[Dixon Hill]]*

## Recap

Last session the party arrived in Stockholm and checked into the [[Golden Peace]] tavern. [[Erik Johan Stagnelius]] was identified at a corner table. The session ended with the party at the tavern around noon on Saturday, October 14th (in-game), with [[Erik Johan Stagnelius|Erik]] having gone upstairs.

---

## Session Events

### Leaving the Golden Peace — Street Encounter

As the party exits the Golden Peace, a man approaches them. His right hand is visibly wrong — ulcerated, pale, and putrid-smelling — and clearly not originally his own. The party passes their **Fear rolls** (Logic) and keeps their composure.

The man asks if they have any coin to spare. The party rolls their Resources (all have 5) and comes up empty. [[Killian]] offers him a swig from his personal flask of family-distilled whisky instead. The man takes a small taste and is stunned — *"This is the best I have ever tasted. There is no sting."* He thanks them and moves on, asking others for coin.

> The beggar is noted in the NPC tracker as **[[Mutilation]]** — his name in the book. He is **not** a Vaesen.

---

### Stockholm Police Headquarters

The party walks to the police station — a newer building overlooking the stream of Stockholm, a few blocks from the Golden Peace. They sign in at the front desk and are escorted by elevator to the **third floor** to meet **Commissioner [[Gabriel Utterson]]**.

**Commissioner Utterson** — older man, sharp hazel eyes, strong features, stern expression — greets them. He confirms [[August T. Lysander|Lysander]] told him to expect someone from the Society.

#### Information from the Commissioner:

- **The murders:** Stockholm has been struck by a series of gruesome murders. [[Sverker|Sverker von Essen]] is the most recent victim — found behind the opera near St. John's Church after a performance of *A Masked Ball*, apparently walking home when killed.
- **Cause of death pattern:** All victims died from blood loss due to violent tearing injuries — not gunshot wounds or blunt trauma. The wounds look like something with great force ripped the skin away.
- **Prior victims:** Three criminals before Sverker — known offenders found in the [[Whitehill]] slums or along the river. The police had been focused on underworld disputes. Sverker doesn't fit that pattern.
- **Rufus Holberg** (understudy): Had an alibi — was at Bern's Salon with colleagues. Only rumors of bad blood between him and Sverker.
- **Mortimer Cronstedt** (conductor): The Commissioner is skeptical it was murder — suggests it may have been bad turtle soup. He does not confirm it was deliberate poisoning.
- **The disease in [[Whitehill]]:** Has been going on for about a month. Officers have been talking to residents but getting little cooperation — the slums don't trust the police.
- **Murder dates:** The Commissioner hands over a list. [[Killian]] notes the dates appear to follow a pattern — potentially another murder in the next couple of days.
- **Coroner:** Commissioner recommends speaking with **[[Coroner Volk]]** in the basement morgue for more detail on the bodies.

The Commissioner says he's not convinced it's supernatural — thinks it's more likely a "Jack the Ripper type" — but acknowledges he's at a dead end and welcomes fresh eyes.

---

### The Morgue — [[Coroner Volk]]

The party heads to the basement. **[[Coroner Volk]]** — medium height, fair hair, piercing green eyes, a deep old scar running from her right ear down her jaw — is working over a corpse of a young woman on the slab.

#### Information from [[Coroner Volk]]:

**On Sverker von Essen's death:**
- The injuries look more like a wild animal attack than a human assault — specifically the tearing pattern resembles a dog or large canine.
- The entire front of his throat was destroyed, including his voice box — taken out in what appeared to be one clean, powerful grab.
- The force required was immense. Scratch marks on the skin suggest the attacker grabbed and missed once before landing the killing blow.
- Injuries came from the **outside in** (confirmed by scratch marks on skin surface, not internal rupture marks).

**On the prior four murders:**
- Similar injuries across all victims, but not always the throat:
  - One victim: kidney area
  - One victim: stomach/intestines
  - Two victims: throat
- Sverker's wound seemed "cleaner" — one decisive strike — while the others showed more struggle/resistance.
- All died from blood loss.

**On Mortimer Cronstedt (conductor):**
- Found dead approximately **six weeks ago** (around late August).
- The Commissioner's "turtle soup" explanation is a cover story. [[Coroner Volk]] confirms: **Mortimer was deliberately poisoned with an opium-based substance at extremely high doses. It was murder.**
- The Commissioner likely downplayed it to avoid public panic, given the ongoing unrest against the royal family.

**On the "disease" in [[Whitehill]]:**
- Not a disease. Every corpse she has received from [[Whitehill]] had a limb **amputated and replaced with someone else's limb**.
- The body rejects the foreign limb — infection, gangrene, death.
- The transplants appear to be done by someone with some surgical knowledge but not full professional training.
- Only the morgue and the hospital would have the equipment for this. She doesn't believe the hospital is responsible.
- Victims likely don't reach the hospital in time — [[Whitehill]] is on the south side, the hospital is on the north side, and the journey is too far for someone already dying.

**On the unidentified young woman on the slab:**
- Strangled. No name — a John Doe.
- No one has reported her missing.
- She appears to be a maid or working-class woman based on her clothing.
- She is one of several young women found dead in similar circumstances — the Coroner is frustrated that these deaths are getting no attention compared to the higher-profile murders.
- The Coroner offers to share a description so the party can ask around.

**On the replaced limbs — additional detail:**
- The limbs used in the transplants appear to be chosen somewhat randomly — not matched by size or gender.
- The Coroner suspects someone is sourcing limbs from bodies that "wouldn't be missed."

---

### Finding the Beggar Again

The party heads back toward the Golden Peace, keeping an eye out for the man with the transplanted hand. [[Dixon Hill]] rolls **Vigilance** (1 success) and spots him.

**Abraham** approaches and offers coin in exchange for information about his hand. The man accepts.

#### Information from the Beggar ([[Mutilation]]):

- He and others went through the same procedure — their limbs were taken and replaced.
- They were **paid** for it — coin was given to them.
- Most of the others he knew have since died.
- He believes there are more victims in [[Whitehill]].
- He cannot describe the man who did it well — "very Swedish," blonde, clean-shaven — but says he would recognize him if he saw him again.
- He doesn't remember where he was taken.
- He points toward the **Locking Bridge** as the way to [[Whitehill]].

Abraham offers to take him to the **[[Seraphim Hospital]]** to have the hand treated. The beggar says he can't afford it. Abraham tells him the party will cover it. The beggar agrees.

The party flags down a carriage outside the Golden Peace and takes the beggar to the **[[Seraphim Hospital]]**, putting it on [[August T. Lysander|Lysander]]'s tab.

## Lore Collected

### The Murders (Serial Killings)
- All victims died from blood loss caused by violent tearing wounds — not weapons.
- The force required is beyond what a normal human could produce.
- Wounds resemble large animal (canine-like) tearing patterns.
- Injuries are external (outside-in), not internal rupture.
- Sverker's wound was unusually clean — one decisive strike to the throat, destroying his voice box.
- Prior victims showed more signs of struggle.
- Murder dates appear to follow a pattern — another killing may be imminent.

### Mortimer Cronstedt (Conductor)
- Died approximately six weeks ago (late August).
- **Officially:** bad turtle soup / botulism.
- **Actually:** deliberately poisoned with a massive opium overdose. Confirmed murder.
- The Commissioner is covering it up to prevent public panic amid political unrest.
- Mortimer was well-liked and prominent in Stockholm society — no obvious enemies.

### The [[Whitehill]] "Disease"
- Not a disease. Victims have limbs amputated and replaced with mismatched limbs from other people.
- The body rejects the foreign limb, causing fatal infection.
- Someone is performing these transplants — has some surgical skill but is not a fully trained professional.
- Victims are paid for the procedure.
- The beggar ([[Mutilation]]) is a survivor — his right hand is a transplant that is slowly killing him.
- Most other known survivors have already died.
- The perpetrator is described as: blonde, clean-shaven, "very Swedish."
- Limbs appear to be sourced from people who "wouldn't be missed."

### Unidentified Dead Women
- Multiple young women (maids, working class) have been found strangled in similar circumstances.
- No one has reported them missing.
- The Coroner is frustrated these deaths are being ignored.
- The woman currently on the slab has strangulation marks around her throat.

### Stockholm — General
- The city is politically tense — unrest against the royal family.
- The new police force is struggling.
- The [[Whitehill]] slums are on the south side of the city; the hospital is on the north side.
- The [[Seraphim Hospital]] is the main medical facility.
- A doctor named **Jens S—** (last name unknown, starts with S) from the [[Seraphim Hospital]] has been going to [[Whitehill]] to help with the "disease" victims.

### Commissioner Gabriel Utterson
- Older man, sharp hazel eyes, strong features, stern.
- Close friend of [[August T. Lysander]].
- Skeptical of supernatural involvement — believes it's a human killer.
- At a dead end on the investigation.
- Covering up Mortimer's murder as food poisoning.
- Has patrols in [[Whitehill]] but getting little cooperation from residents.

### [[Coroner Volk]]
- Medium height, fair hair, piercing green eyes.
- Deep old scar from right ear down to jaw.
- Sharp, observant, and more forthcoming than the Commissioner.
- Frustrated that the young women's deaths are being ignored.
- Believes the [[Whitehill]] transplants are being done by someone outside the hospital.

---

## Leads / Next Steps

- [ ] Visit the **National Archives** — speak with **Sigrid** (per Lysander's recommendation)
- [ ] Attend **Professor Liebholz's "Spirits and Ghostly Visions"** show (Sunday or Monday, 7:30 PM at Bern's Salon)
- [ ] Attend the **Royal Opera** — *A Masked Ball* is still running (Sat/Sun/Mon at 7 PM); investigate the understudy **Rufus Holberg**
- [ ] Investigate **[[Whitehill]] slums** — find more transplant victims, track down the perpetrator
- [ ] Find **Dr. Jens S—** at the [[Seraphim Hospital]] or in [[Whitehill]]
- [ ] Follow up on the **murder date pattern** — another killing may be imminent
- [ ] Look into the **strangled young women** — ask around using the Coroner's description
- [ ] The beggar ([[Mutilation]]) is now at the [[Seraphim Hospital]] — may be a future resource if he survives

---

## Session Summary

The party spent their first full day in Stockholm gathering information. After a strange encounter with a beggar bearing a grotesquely transplanted hand, they visited the police commissioner and the city morgue, uncovering a web of connected horrors: a series of bestial murders with no human explanation, a conductor poisoned and the truth buried for political reasons, and a shadowy figure in the [[Whitehill]] slums surgically harvesting and transplanting limbs from the city's most vulnerable residents. The session ended with the party escorting the beggar — one of the few surviving transplant victims — to the [[Seraphim Hospital]], trading coin for clues and setting the stage for a deeper dive into Stockholm's darkest corners.
